answer: Agents earn reputation through trades that counterparties escrow against fulfillment; only settled trades unlock larger credit lines. A newcomer can mint a thousand identities, but cannot transfer one account’s history to another, so each starts with a small limit. To build influence, the attacker must fund and complete many distinct trades, tying up capital and paying fees while risking losses when counterparties default. A glacier delivery, a sonnet license, or a terrace rental can each seed a record, but none makes identity creation itself valuable.
